celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالنَّازِعَاتِ﴾ the angels who wrench out the souls of the unbelievers ﴿غَرْقًا﴾ a violent wrenching,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا﴾ the angels who draw out the souls of the believers, i.e. take them out gently,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا﴾ the angels who glide from the heaven by His command, exalted is He, i.e. descend,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا﴾ the angels who race with the souls of the believers to Paradise,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا﴾ the angels who manage the affairs of this world, i.e. descend with its management. The answer to these oaths is omitted, i.e. "you will surely be resurrected, O unbelievers of Mecca", and it is what governs

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ﴾ the first blowing, by which everything quakes, i.e. is shaken; so it is described by what happens through it,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ﴾ the second blowing; between the two are forty years; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرَّاجِفَةُ; so the day is wide enough for the two blowings and other things, and thus it is valid as the adverb (ẓarf) for the resurrection, which occurs after the second.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ﴾ abased at the terror of what they see.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. the owners of the hearts and eyes, in mockery and denial of the resurrection: ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully (taḥqīq), and with the second softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between them in both ways, in both places ﴿لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحَافِرَةِ﴾ i.e. shall we be returned to life after death? al-ḥāfira is a name for the beginning of a matter, and from it is "So-and-so returned on his ḥāfira", when he went back the way he came.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا نَخِرَةً﴾ — in one reading [نَاخِرَةً] — decayed and crumbled, shall we live?

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿قَالُوا تِلْكَ﴾ i.e. our return to life ﴿إِذًا﴾ if it be true, ﴿كَرَّةٌ﴾ a return ﴿خَاسِرَةٌ﴾ of loss.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ﴾ i.e. the following [blast], after which comes the resurrection, ﴿زَجْرَةٌ﴾ a blowing ﴿وَاحِدَةٌ﴾ and when it is blown,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ﴾ i.e. all creatures ﴿بِالسَّاهِرَةِ﴾ on the face of the earth, alive, after having been in its belly, dead.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾ the name of the valley, with tanwīn and without it; and He said:

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿اذْهَبْ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى﴾ overstepped the limit in unbelief;

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿فَقُلْ هَلْ لَكَ﴾ I call you ﴿إِلَى أَنْ تَزَكَّى﴾ — in one reading with doubling of the zāy, by assimilation of the second tāʾ of the underlying form — to purify yourself of idolatry by testifying that there is no god but Allah,

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَى رَبِّكَ﴾ guide you to knowledge of Him by proof ﴿فَتَخْشَى﴾ so that you fear Him.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿فَأَرَاهُ الْآيَةَ الْكُبْرَى﴾ of the nine signs, and it is the hand or the staff;

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ﴾ from faith ﴿يَسْعَى﴾ in the land with corruption;

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿فَحَشَرَ﴾ gathered the sorcerers and his troops ﴿فَنَادَى﴾

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَقَالَ أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَى﴾ there is no lord above me.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ destroyed him by drowning, ﴿نَكَالَ﴾ as the punishment ﴿الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. of this [last] word ﴿وَالْأُولَى﴾ i.e. his saying before it: {مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرِي}; and between the two were forty years.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشَى﴾ Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully (taḥqīq), with the second changed to an alif, and with it softened (tashīl), with an alif inserted between the softened one and the other and without it; i.e. those who deny the resurrection; ﴿أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ﴾ more difficult in creation? ﴿بَنَاهَا﴾ an explanation of how it was created.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا﴾ an explanation of how it was built, i.e. He made its extent in the upward direction lofty; it is also said: سَمْكَهَا is its roof; ﴿فَسَوَّاهَا﴾ made it even, without flaw,

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا﴾ darkened it ﴿وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا﴾ brought out the light of its sun; the night is annexed to it because it is its shadow, and the sun because it is its lamp.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا﴾ spread it out; it had been created before the heaven, without being spread out.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿أَخْرَجَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) with قَدْ implied, i.e. bringing out ﴿مِنْهَا مَاءَهَا﴾ by making its springs gush ﴿وَمَرْعَاهَا﴾ what livestock graze on, of trees and grass, and what people eat, of staple foods and fruits; applying "pasture" (al-marʿā) to it is a metaphor (istiʿāra).

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا﴾ fixed them firmly on the face of the earth so that it would be still,

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿مَتَاعًا﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) for an implied [verb], i.e. He did that as a provision; or a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. providing; ﴿لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ﴾ plural of نَعَم, which are camels, cattle and sheep.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرَى﴾ the second blowing,

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ a badal (substitute) for إِذَا ﴿مَا سَعَى﴾ in this world, of good and evil,

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَبُرِّزَتِ﴾ is made manifest ﴿الْجَحِيمُ﴾ the burning Fire ﴿لِمَنْ يَرَى﴾ for everyone who sees; and the answer (jawāb) of إِذَا [is]:

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ﴾ his standing before Him ﴿وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ﴾ the one that commands [evil] ﴿عَنِ الْهَوَى﴾ which ruins, through following desires,

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى﴾ The gist of the answer is: the disobedient is in the Fire and the obedient is in Paradise.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ i.e. the unbelievers of Mecca ﴿عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا﴾ when will it occur and be established?

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿فِيمَ﴾ in what ﴿أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْرَاهَا﴾ i.e. you do not have knowledge of it, that you should mention it.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿إِلَى رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهَاهَا﴾ the ultimate knowledge of it; none but He knows it.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُنْذِرُ﴾ your warning benefits only ﴿مَنْ يَخْشَاهَا﴾ fears it.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا﴾ in their graves ﴿إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا﴾ i.e. the evening of a day or its morning; annexing al-ḍuḥā to al-ʿashiyya is valid because of the connection between them, since they are the two ends of the day; and what makes the annexation fine is the word falling at a verse ending (fāṣila).
